name: transparent overlay autotile for the edges of a cracked concrete slab pavement on dirt: only the broken edge is drawn — rounded dirt bites eaten into the concrete from the open sides, a dark 1px broken lip under south breaks, lit broken rims, and loose concrete chunks lying on the dirt; the slab field underneath shows through so its seams and cracks run right up to the break
label: wasteland_ruins/slab-break

surfaces.part: concrete slab fragments (largest is the broken slab at right, with seams and cracks) seen flat from above
dark 1px broken lip under south-facing breaks
surfaces.rows: 1 row under each south break, e.g. row 108

surfaces.part: loose concrete chunks and small dirt-coloured pebbles on the dirt

answer.evidence: This is a transparent edge overlay over a full-width dirt field (width 256 on every row). The concrete pieces are flat plates seen from above, with seams and cracks drawn in plan view. There is no raised volume, no ellipse and no roof or awning plane. The only vertical-looking element is the 1px dark lip under the south breaks, which is an outline-like edge and not a front face of 3 or more rows. The main body therefore has no front face, so it reads as a flat top-down slab, which is consistent with the flat decal kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts support a pass. The candidate has 5 visible tones per tile, above the grass reference (3) and below the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. 0% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the lips and seams are tinted rather than a black sticker line. By eye, the concrete chunks show speckle, a lighter lit rim, dark seams and cracks, and a dark lip. The dirt has clumped dark patches. The concrete ramp is about 5 steps (highlight, light, mid, seam, deep lip), slightly under the paving reference. With only 12 total colours the dirt texture is somewhat repetitive. Overall it sits slightly below the paving reference but would be acceptable beside it.

answer.evidence: This is a 256x192 flat autotile sheet: a dirt field with concrete slab patches seen straight down. The slab surfaces, with their seams and cracks, are flat plates. The only south-facing depth is a 1px dark broken lip under the south breaks, and the right-hand large patch is the biggest slab at roughly rows 19-109. That gives no front face of 3 or more rows, no eave and no ellipse, so it is a flat top-down decal, which is correct for kind flat.

styleAnswer.evidence: The concrete reads as about 4 steps: light rim, mid speckled grey, darker grey, and a dark seam or lip. The dirt has about 3-4 brown tones with dark clod spots. This is a bit shallower than Beodeul's 5-6 steps, but it is a transparent edge overlay, so the lower count is plausible. Measured facts: 5 visible tones per tile sits between the grass reference (3) and the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 0%, and 0% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the broken edges and seams carry a tint rather than a black sticker line. The paving reference itself has only 7 raw colours, so the candidate's 12 total is not shallow by comparison. Texture comes from speckled concrete, cracks, chunk dots and clumpy dirt, with no large flat fills. The craft is slightly less layered than the references but acceptable beside them.

surfaces.part: dirt ground with concrete slab fragments (flat overlay)

answer.evidence: This is a flat top-down ground decal. The concrete fragments, dirt bites and seams are all seen from above. The only vertical-looking detail is a 1px dark broken lip under south-facing breaks, which is an outline-like edge and not a front face of 3 or more rows. The column scan shows no tall front face, no eave shadow band and no ellipse. The scan's dark 1-row runs (e.g. rows 24-25, 89) are seams or lips, not a front face. There is no side face and no standing volume, so it reads as a flat plate, as the kind requires.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 5 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edges. That is above the grass reference (3 tones) and below the paving reference (7 tones). The outline is tinted, not a black sticker line: a dark lip sits only under the south breaks, and forms are otherwise separated by value. The concrete chunks use about 4 steps (light rim, mid, speckle, dark seam or lip) against 5-6 in the references. The whole piece has only 12 distinct colours. The dirt reads as repeated dark clump marks on a flat brown base, and the concrete speckle is a sparse two-tone dither. There are no per-stone shades or clumps like the references. Next to the paving reference, the chunks look slightly thinner and flatter. They are clean and well structured, but fall short of Beodeul richness, so I fail it on doubt.

surfaces.part: cracked concrete slab fragments (overlay break edges)
dirt bites, broken lip and loose chunks

answer.evidence: This is a flat autotile overlay sheet seen straight down: a dirt field with grey concrete slab fragments on it. The only vertical element is a 1px dark broken lip under the south breaks, and the column scan shows no front face of 3+ rows. Seams and cracks run across the slab surface. It matches the 'top-down slab (no front)' guide pattern, which is acceptable for a flat decal.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 12 distinct colours in total and 5 visible tones per tile. That is above the grass reference (3) but below the paving reference (7). The concrete chunks read as about 3 grey steps (light rim, mid grey, darker seam or lip) with a speckle dither. The Beodeul paving has about 6-7 steps with per-stone shading. The dirt is a mottled 3-4 tone brown with small dark pits, which is acceptable texture, but the whole material ramp is shallow. The edges are mostly value-separated, and the dark lip is a tinted grey-brown rather than pure black (0% neutral dark edge pixels), so the outline is not a sticker line. The concrete pieces are blocky and fairly tiny, with little of the rounded dirt bite shaping and no clear lit rim or dark south lip on most pieces. The large slab at right has some flat-looking grey areas with a faint speckle. Overall it is competent, but its shading depth and tile detail sit below the references. When in doubt, fail.
